newsitem.title: USA: Spreads on 10-year US swaps squeezing dealers.
newsitem.headline: Spreads on 10-year US swaps squeezing dealers.

text.p: Spreads on 10-year U.S. interest rate swaps remained at historically tight levels on Monday, putting a squeeze on dealers who bet spreads would widen.

Early on Monday, dealers long on the 10-year spread thought their salvation had arrived when the on-the-run 10-year Treasury note was listed on special in the repurchase market. When notes are cheap to borrow in the repo market, dealers can buy notes and hedge with swaps, pushing spreads wider. But the repo special quickly faded and spreads on 10-year swaps stayed locked at the 33 basis point level.
The 10-year spread has been well below 40 basis points for months, dealers noted, and tightened by two to three basis points in the past week.
Traders said heavy bond issuance was to blame for the tightness. Eurobond issuers selling dollar-denominated deals swap to floating, pushing spreads tighter.

One New York dealer said a $400 million trade overnight was bid aggressively. The firm that won the business "was back in the market today hammering spreads," the dealer said. With so much business on one side of the market, the difference between bids and offers is less than a basis point, he said.
Bond issuance and related swapping is expected to continue but one swap trader said swap spreads could ease if the next month's 10-year note auction sparks a longer-lived repo special.
The firm pushing down the overnight repo rate Monday was said to be looking for term repo trades through the settlement date of the upcoming 10-year auction in mid-November.
"It depends how they line up at the auction, but there does seem to be a move in that direction," the trader said. "Until then, it's more of the same."
At the short-end, spreads widened by up to two basis points over the past week after narrowing slightly on the September producer price index report.
On two-year LIBOR swaps, spreads were quoted Monday at 17 basis points bid, 19 to 20 basis points offered, about two basis points wider than a week earlier.
The upcoming two-year note auction on Tuesday had no discernable impact on spreads, traders said.
On three-year swaps, spreads were quoted at 20 basis points bid, 21 to 22 basis points offered, about one basis point tighter.
Five-year swap spreads felt tightening pressure from bond issuance, dealers said.
Monday, spreads were quoted at 23 basis points bid, 25 to 26 basis points offered, about two basis points tighter than a week earlier.
